title: Skill Relationship Map
description: Machine-readable map of relationships and dependencies between user-level and Ai-Vault project-level skills. Includes relationship types required by Story-01-05 and maps each to candidate Agent Graph edge types, with notes when the mapping is approximate (because the Agent Graph spec does not yet define skill→skill edge types beyond tool/workflow/agent usage). Curators should treat each skill's references/skill-escalation.md as primary boundary evidence when present.

notes: The Agent Graph spec currently enumerates Tool/Workflow/Agent edges from a Skill node, but does not explicitly define a Skill→Skill edge type. This map therefore uses candidate edges like `depends_on` (mentioned as an example in Story-01-05) to represent Skill→Skill relationships, and marks those mappings as approximate.

high_risk_refactor_sequences.why_high_risk: Multiple downstream skills explicitly compose with deep-research; refactoring deep-research workflows/tooling likely breaks many consumers.
suggested_safe_sequence: Add compatibility shim layer to deep-research outputs (stable report schema / template).
Refactor and validate downstream consumers one-by-one (documentation → web-visual → market-segmentation → document-deep-merge → research-analysis).
Only then change deep-research core prompts/workflow steps.

high_risk_refactor_sequences.shared_capability: Atlassian/Confluence/Jira MCP wiring (user-mcp-atlassian or equivalent tool surface)
high_risk_refactor_sequences.why_high_risk: At least two skills rely on Confluence/Jira search/fetch/create/update semantics; changing tool names/parameters breaks both sync and knowledge-search flows.
suggested_safe_sequence: Introduce a stable adapter interface for Atlassian operations (search/get/update/create) and migrate both skills to that adapter.
Refactor obsidian-confluence-sync scripts/MCP workflows with integration tests (diff/push/pull) before changing any destructive operations.
Then refactor search-company-knowledge tool invocation naming (search/getConfluencePage/getJiraIssue) to match the adapter.

high_risk_refactor_sequences.why_high_risk: diagram is a common visualization dependency; kion-design and documentation/document-deep-merge rely on it for diagram lifecycle steps, making format/adapter changes broadly impactful.
suggested_safe_sequence: Stabilize the diagram semantic model and adapter contracts first (draw.io default, Excalidraw fallback).
Then validate branding overlays (kion-design tokens) and doc embedding flows (documentation, document-deep-merge).

high_risk_refactor_sequences.why_high_risk: project-planning consumes specification artifacts; changes to spec storage layout or output conventions cascade into planning workflows and downstream VC expectations.
suggested_safe_sequence: Keep spec output paths and templates backward compatible (or provide migration scripts).
When changing spec output paths, update manifest source_globs and sample traces_to; keep legacy --project layout working.
